The Muslim subjects of the Lodis were required to pay the zakat tax for religious merit, and the non-Muslims were required to pay the jizya tax for receiving state protection.  In some parts of the Sultanate, the Hindus were required to pay an additional pilgrimage tax.  Nevertheless, several Hindu officers formed a part of the Sultanate's revenue administration.  Sikandar Khan Lodi, whose mother was a Hindu, resorted to strong Sunni orthodoxy to prove his Islamic credentials as a political expediency.
